conceptZh: 科學家老鼠的蝴蝶網有自己的想法，亂甩亂飛，直到他輕輕一舉才網住蝶字的筆畫。
object: a bespectacled lab mouse with a mischievous butterfly net
morph: a net with its own opinion flings glittery pieces around until the mouse outsmarts it into 蝶
creativeAngle: 道具反抗：網子一直把筆畫甩開，老鼠改用輕輕一勾才成功。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a pale lavender-pink background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 蝶 as the only text on screen, drawn in violet purple solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a bespectacled lab mouse in a tiny white coat swings a long-handled net that bends the wrong way and flings him in a circle; the first 蝶 is spoken as the left 虫 strokes flutter in like glittery wing-dust. 1.7-3.4s: the net slaps a bubbling beaker so it fizzes over and tosses the right-hand 枼 pieces across the frame; the second 蝶 is spoken as the mouse lowers the net gently, stops fighting it, and the pieces drift in one by one. 3.4-5s: 蝴蝶 is spoken as a shimmering lilac toy butterfly flaps out of the net, circles his head, and lands on his glasses, making him cross his eyes. 5-8s: hold; the butterfly opens and closes its wings on the mouse's nose, glyph still. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蝶、蝶、蝴蝶" (ㄉㄧㄝˊ、ㄉㄧㄝˊ、ㄏㄨˊ ㄉㄧㄝˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 蝶 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
